basis: Assumption: the softest of the race's three dry compounds. A car in the wake loses front downforce, slides more and runs hotter tyre surfaces; a softer compound has a lower working window and overheats sooner, so the same wake costs a little more. A small per-lap sensitivity multiplier on the race's assumed loss, NOT tyre wear (wear builds over a stint and is not modelled here)
Reference (1.00): the race's middle dry compound. The race value is read as the cost on the middle compound

Assumption: the hardest of the race's three dry compounds. It tolerates the extra sliding and heat of following better, so the same wake costs slightly less. Smaller step than SOFT because a hard tyre still slides when following; 0.96 not 0.95 because 0.95 makes some race x tyre values equal an archived-method number at 3 dp (BUILD-ORDER rule 6)

Neutral: the dry-compound softness ranking does not extend to intermediate tyres (different construction, cooled by standing water) and there is no basis to rank them, so the race value is used unchanged and the lap is flagged
Neutral: as for INTERMEDIATE. In the wet the wake's main cost is spray and visibility, which this placeholder does not model; the race value is used unchanged and the lap is flagged
